**Text:**

HFrEF treatment algorithm (synthetic summary)

Stage C HFrEF: LVEF 40% or lower, symptoms present or prior

Start all four pillars within 6 weeks:
ARNI (or ACEI/ARB) + beta-blocker + MRA + SGLT2i
add loop diuretic for congestion

Reassess LVEF after 3 months
of optimized GDMT

LVEF 35% or lower,
NYHA II-III,
life expectancy >1 year:
ICD

LVEF 35% or lower,
LBBB with QRS 150 ms
or longer, sinus rhythm:
CRT-D

Persistent NYHA IV
despite GDMT (Stage D):
refer for LVAD or
transplant evaluation

Also: SGLT2i is started regardless of diabetes status, titrate to target doses every 2 weeks as tolerated.
Hydrochlorothiazide + isosorbide dinitrate: add for self-identified Black patients with NYHA III-IV on optimal GDMT.


**Description:**

The figure illustrates a treatment algorithm for Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction (HFrEF) – Stage C, defined as an LVEF of 40% or lower with symptoms present. The algorithm begins with the initiation of four key pillars of therapy: an ARNI (or ACEi/ARB), a beta-blocker, a mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (MRA), and a sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitor (SGLT2i), alongside a loop diuretic for congestion management.  After 3 months of optimized guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT), the LVEF is reassessed, and the flowchart branches based on the LVEF value and presence of specific arrhythmias (LBBB with QRS >150ms or sinus rhythm) or persistent NYHA IV symptoms, directing the patient to specific interventions like CRT-D or LVAD/transplant evaluation.  Finally, the algorithm includes specific considerations for Black patients with NYHA III-IV on optimal GDMT, recommending the addition of hydrochlorothiazide and isosorbide dinitrate.
